answer: At a saffron terrace, buyers pay agents to relay a signal from soil sensors. Each relay answers a fresh random challenge from two independently chosen receivers within a latency window; one challenge ID pays once, regardless of sender identity. Aliases on one machine cannot replay a packet for extra fees. To claim more work, an attacker needs more low-latency links and deposits at risk if samples disagree. Colluding receivers or rented nearby servers can still fake diverse paths, so receivers rotate and occasional physical audits remain necessary.
